input.quote: (a) as soon as reasonably practicable, destroy all copies of such Confidential Information in the possession of the other Party and confirm such destruction in writing to the requesting Party; or (b) as soon as reasonably practicable, deliver to the requesting Party, at such other Party's expense, all copies of such Confidential Information in the possession of such other Party
input.rationale: The Agreement contains usable exit machinery covering both limbs of this rule, and the direction favours us on the data limb. Section 9.7 (p0517–p0518) is a mutual, termination-triggered return-or-destroy right exercisable at the requesting Party's written election, with written certification of destruction where deletion is chosen, and it expressly limits the other Party's retention to one archival/legal-compliance copy plus automated back-ups — that is the preferred "return, then delete and certify" construct, applied in our favour against Harpoon as well as against us. The wind-down/transition limb is covered by Section 12.6.1(c) and Article 12.7 (reversion of Harpoon Reversion Products, transfer of Regulatory Documentation and data, and AbbVie assistance as Harpoon reasonably requests), by the post-termination sell-off period in Section 12.10.2, and by surviving Section 3.8.5 (p0331), which continues Harpoon's record-retention and AbbVie's right to copies after termination. Note also that Harpoon's forward-looking transfer and assistance obligations sit in Sections 3.5, 3.8.2(a) and 4.5.2 (full Manufacturing Technology Transfer with reasonable assistance, continuing at AbbVie's request against reimbursement) — the "help moving" that this rule protects is already ours. Direction check: the exit transfer/destruction obligations in Article 12.7 and Section 12.6.1(c) run from AbbVie to Harpoon because rights in the Licensed Compounds revert to Harpoon on termination; that is inherent in the option/licence bargain, not a vendor-side gap, and inserting a Vendor data-return clause would be inapposite since Harpoon holds no AbbVie-owned service data as a processor. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: Section 9.7 uses "as soon as reasonably practicable" instead of a fixed thirty-day export window, and specifies no machine-readable format; and Section 12.6.1(c) lets Harpoon elect destruction of AbbVie-generated data (though Section 12.10.2's sell-off period and Section 9.7's retained archival copy blunt this, and it is not immediate deletion of our own data). On its material terms the clause set meets the fallback and substantially the preferred position, so no redline.
